text:
Nadia: deploy-bot just flagged a regression during the eu-dedicated change window. embeddings drifted; quick check before we auto-unwind? :eyes:

deploy-bot: DEPLOYBOT: Canary alert for release v2.4.0-quantb. Metrics: embeddings_similarity -4.8% vs baseline, p95 latency +140ms, error_rate unchanged. Canary traffic: 30%. Recommendation: HOLD AND ROLLBACK CONSIDERED. Generated 2025-05-02T09:12:12Z.

Jorge: How many tenants hit the canary slice? Any high-tier customers affected?

Priya: Two midmarket customers routed through eu-dedicated canary. No active escalations yet. SLAs look untouched but we shouldn't risk it during the window.

Tom: I see degraded kv hit ratio and a small spike in GC on eu-host-7. Not seeing exceptions; perf degradation likely from quantization mismatch for short queries.

Nadia: My read: severity is moderate. Since change window auto-rollbacks are off, we need a manual decision + clear comms. Options: 1) Pin back to v2.3.9 (pre-quant) and drain canary; 2) Gradual rollback with traffic split to 0 over 10m; 3) Leave canary but throttle traffic and investigate. Thoughts?

Priya: Prefer full pin and drain. Graceful traffic split leaves risk of noisy samples continuing to feed metrics.

Tom: Agree with pin+drain. Also suggest adding a temporary routing rule to exclude the two midmarket tenants until we validate.

Jorge: I'll prepare customer note draft if we rollback. Legal-Bot: do we need to notify compliance for possible SLA notices?

Legal-Bot: No legal escalation required at this time. Notify if any customer reports or SLA breaches occur. Archive message for audit.

Nadia: Decision: manual rollback. Action items: Jorge to prepare customer note, Tom to execute routing pin+drain, Priya to update incident ticket, Nadia to update release notes and schedule a postmortem.

Tom: Executing now. Commands: ```
# pin eu-dedicated to v2.3.9
redwoodctl routes set --region eu --pool dedicated --model v2.3.9 --pin --reason "rollback-20250502"
# drain canary deploy
redwoodctl deploy scale --id deploy-eu-20250502-quantb --target 0 --grace 300
# add tenant exclusion
redwoodctl routes exclude --tenant tenant-471,tenant-522 --pool eu-dedicated
```

deploy-bot: DEPLOYBOT: Manual action recorded by @Tom. Canary traffic adjusted to 0% for v2.4.0-quantb. Hooks: observability, billing, evals. Estimated completion 8 minutes.

Priya: Drain completed on eu-dedicated pool; v2.4.0-quantb pods terminated cleanly. p95 latency returned to baseline. Exclusions applied.

SRE-Oncall: Filed INC-20250502-embdrift. Tagging for postmortem. Please attach quant config and short-query eval slices.

Jorge: Drafted customer note: "During a scheduled change window we observed a temporary drop in embedding similarity for a canary release. We have rolled back the model for the affected region and are monitoring. No customer data was accessed or exposed. We'll follow up with a timeline for re-release after verification." Posting to #cust-notices after get sign-off from Nadia.

Nadia: Approved. Jorge, publish and link the notice in the incident ticket. Also: block auto-quant gate for eu region until we've run the targeted evals and canary pass.

Tom: Gate blocked. Command: ```
redwoodctl feature-gates set --region eu --feature auto-quant --state off --reason "post-rollback-eval"
```

Priya: Running regression harness now against short-query slices; pushing results to eval dashboard. ETA ~90m.

Nadia: Thanks team. We'll reconvene after the evals. For runbook: include the deploy-bot suggestion, manual pin steps, tenant exclusion, and who to CC for customer comms. Closing thread for execution; reopen if metrics deviate. :lock:

Jorge: Publishing customer note now. Link: https://internal.gov/notes/INC-20250502-embdrift

Tom: Post-rollback checks green. Leaving pin for 2 hours per change-window policy then reassess.
